Appearance: Leaves are perfectly formed, lanceolate to oval shape, and highly uniform in size (averaging 3-4 cm long).
Color: Deep, vibrant, uniform dark green color on the top surface with a noticeably paler, matte underside. No yellowing or black spots.
Texture/Maturity: Predominantly young leaves; glossy, taut, crisp, and pliable. Smooth edges. Leaves are tender and only slightly chewy.

Appearance: Leaves are mostly well-formed, with slight variation in size. Minimal broken or torn leaves.

Stem Structure: Mostly individual leaves or very small, incomplete clusters.
Aroma & Flavor: Weak, stale, or dusty fragrance. The pungent flavor is faint, and bitterness is more pronounced than the herbal notes.

Appearance: High percentage of broken fragments, dust, or foreign matter. Signs of mold or decay.

Structure: The umbels are perfectly formed, flat, and wide-spreading. The slender pedicels are upright and intact, showing no signs of crushing.
Color: The petals exhibit a vibrant, uniform golden yellow or bright yellow-green hue with no browning.
Texture: The blossoms are highly succulent and tender with a noticeable "subtle crisp" snap when handled.
Aroma: The aroma is intense, fresh, and distinctly herbal immediately upon inspection.
Flavor: The flavor is robust and complex; the sour characteristic is punchy, followed immediately by a clear, pleasant sweet finish. The citrus and anise notes are bright.

Structure: The umbels are generally intact, though the wide-spreading formation may be slightly less symmetrical. Pedicels remain largely sturdy.
Color: Good color saturation in the yellow/yellow-green range, though lacking the intense "glow" of the Excellent tier.
Texture: Texture remains tender and soft, but the "subtle crispness" is diminished. They are still succulent.
Aroma: Fresh herbal aroma is present but requires closer inspection to detect fully.
Flavor: The flavor profile is characteristic (sour/herbal), but the "sweet finish" is less pronounced or shorter-lived.

Structure: The umbels may look slightly compressed or messy. Some pedicels may be bent, disrupting the flat-topped appearance.
Color: The yellow is fading to a pale straw color or looking washed out; the green undertones are dull.
Texture: The blossoms are soft but lack succulence; they feel slightly limp or dry rather than crisp.
Aroma: The fresh herbal scent is faint; a generic "grassy" smell begins to replace the specific dill aroma.
Flavor: The robust nature is lost; the flavor is mild. The sourness is present, but the complex anise/celery nuances are difficult to distinguish.

Structure: The umbels are drooping significantly. Pedicels are limp or tangled, making the cluster look collapsed.
Color: Visible discoloration; petals are turning beige or have brown edges.
Texture: The texture is flaccid (loss of turgidity) or becoming tough/chewy rather than tender.
Aroma: Very weak aroma, or identifying a slight "hay-like" or dried herb smell.
Flavor: Flavor is flat and largely tasteless, or strictly sour without any sweetness or citrus brightness.

Structure: The umbels are crushed, broken, or decomposing. Flowers have fallen off the pedicels.
Color: Dark brown, black, or greyish spots indicating rot or severe oxidation.
Texture: Slimy/mushy (rotting) or completely brittle/desiccated (dried out).
Aroma: Unpleasant, musty, moldy, or sour-rot smell.
Flavor: Bitter, rancid, or inedible.

Appearance (Leaves): Leaves are vibrant, deep green, and stand upright. The "wispy" structure is distinct and separated, not clumped.
Appearance (Flowers): If flowering, the umbels are bright yellow and intact, forming a perfect flat-topped cluster.
Aroma: Pungent, fresh, and zesty. The sour, pickle-like scent is immediately apparent without crushing.
Flavor: Complex and potent. The notes of anise, celery, and the lemon finish are perfectly balanced and distinct.
Texture: Turgid and crisp; stems snap easily.

Appearance (Leaves): Green color is consistent but may lack the intense sheen of the 'Excellent' grade.
Appearance (Flowers): Flowers are yellow but may show very slight wilting at the edges of the cluster.
Aroma: Strong characteristic aroma, though it may require slight handling to release the full bouquet.
Flavor: The anise and parsley notes are clear, though the lemon finish might be slightly less sharp.
Texture: Mostly crisp, though the fern-like leaves may be slightly softer.

Appearance (Leaves): Leaves appear dull green. There is no yellowing, but the "wispy" leaves may be slightly matted or drooping.
Appearance (Flowers): Flowers appear faded yellow or are beginning to drop petals.
Aroma: The fresh sour scent is weak; smells more generally "grassy" or herbaceous than distinctively like dill.
Flavor: Flavor is present but mild; the specific notes (anise/lemon) are difficult to distinguish individually.
Texture: Leaves are limp or beginning to wilt; stems bend rather than snap.

Appearance (Leaves): Visible yellowing on the tips of the fern-like leaves. The plant looks tired.
Appearance (Flowers): Umbels are browning or drying out significantly.
Aroma: Very faint scent, or a slight "hay-like" or dried smell replacing the fresh aroma.
Flavor: Flavor is flat and weak. The lemon finish is entirely absent.
Texture: Flaccid and limp. The wispy structure has collapsed.

Appearance (Leaves): Dark, black, or slimy leaves. significant decomposition or browning.
Appearance (Flowers): Brown, shriveled, or rot evident in the flower clusters.
Aroma: Unpleasant, musty, or smelling of decay/rot rather than fresh pickles.
Flavor: Unpalatable, bitter, or rancid.
Texture: Slimy, mushy, or completely dried out and brittle (depending on storage conditions).

Foliage Appearance: Leaves are vibrant, deep green, and highly turgid. The "wrinkled" texture is deep and distinct, indicating high water content. The "toothed" edges are sharp and crisp.
Stem Condition: Stems are green, succulent, and clearly square in cross-section. They support the bushy habit without bending.
Leaf Surface: Whether the specific variant is "smooth" or "hairy," the surface is clean and uniform. If hairy, the fuzz is soft, not matted.
Flower State: Ideally harvested before full bloom for culinary leaf quality. If flowers are present, they are tight, fresh white buds in the axils, not shedding.
Pests: Absolutely no insects present, despite being a "good nectar source.

Foliage Appearance: Consistent green color. Leaves are heart-shaped/oval but may be slightly less uniform in size.
Texture: The wrinkled surface is present, but leaves may feel slightly softer (less rigid) than the Excellent tier.
Stem Condition: Stems retain the square shape but may show signs of becoming fibrous near the base.
Flower State: Flowers may be open (pale yellow/purple) but look fresh and vibrant.
General: The bushy habit is preserved; the bunch does not look leggy.

Foliage Appearance: Leaves appear dull or olive-green. The "toothed" edges may be curling slightly.
Texture: Leaves feel flat (loss of the wrinkled 3D texture) or slightly dry/papery.
Stem Condition: Stems are becoming woody, tough, or turning brown.
Flower State: Flowers are fully open and beginning to brown or drop petals, making the clusters look messy.
General: The plant looks sparse, with more stem visible than leaf.

Foliage Appearance: Significant yellowing (chlorosis) or browning on the leaf tips.
Texture: Leaves are limp, flaccid, or leathery. The hairy varieties may feel dusty or rough.
Stem Condition: Stems are hard, woody sticks that snap dryly or bend without breaking (leathery).
Flower State: Flowers are dried out, brown, and seeding.
Aroma: (Implicit) Weak or hay-like smell replacing the fresh scent.

Foliage Appearance: Black, dark brown, or grey (mold).
Texture: Slimy/wet (rot) or crumbling into dust (desiccated).
Stem Condition: Black, moldy, or covered in webs.
General: Evidence of insect infestation (bees/bugs still attached) or foreign weeds mixed in.
Smell: Musty, mildewy, or sour.

Appearance (Stems): The base of the stems is a pristine, bright white transitioning smoothly to green. There is absolutely no red, purple, or maroon discoloration (matching the "entirely green or white" requirement).
Appearance (Leaves): Leaves are a vibrant, healthy bluish-green. They are long, strap-shaped, and exhibit the characteristic "graceful droop" at the tips without being limp.
Texture: The leaf edges feel distinctively rough and "serrated" when run through fingers (carefully), indicating high structural integrity.
Scent: The fresh, lemon-like fragrance is immediate and clean upon the slightest bruising.
Moisture: Stems are turgid, heavy, and juicy.

Appearance (Stems): Base is white/green. Very minor blemishes or slight dullness in the white section are acceptable, but still no red pigmentation.
Appearance (Leaves): Good green color, though the distinct "bluish" hue may be less intense (more of a standard light green).
Texture: Leaves are rough to the touch, though the serration might feel slightly worn or less sharp.
Scent: Distinct lemon fragrance is present but requires active crushing to release fully.
Moisture: Stems are firm but may yield slightly under strong pressure.

Appearance (Stems): The white base is turning beige or creamy-yellow (oxidation). The "green" upper sections are dull.
Appearance (Leaves): Leaves are losing the "strap shape" and becoming curled or dried at the tips (brown tips >1 cm).
Texture: The "rough" edges are becoming brittle. The leaf blade feels papery rather than fibrous/live.
Scent: The aroma is mild to weak. The "fresh" lemon note is fading, replaced by a generic grassy smell.
General: Clumps appear loose or thinning rather than "dense.

Appearance (Stems): Significant browning or scarring on the lower stalks. The plant looks tired/old.
Appearance (Leaves): Yellowing (chlorosis) extending down the leaf blade. The "graceful droop" has turned into a "wilted collapse."
Texture: Leaves are dry and harsh rather than live/rough. Stems are woody and tough.
Scent: Very faint. Smells more like hay or dried straw than lemon.
Defect: Presence of reddish/purple hues at the base (indicating potential cross-contamination with other varieties or stress).

Visual Appearance: Leaves are a rich, lustrous "vivid to dark green." If the specific variety includes purple/bronze blushing, it is distinct and vibrant, not brownish.
Structure: Leaves are perfectly oval with sharp, clearly defined serrated edges. The "veined" surface is deep and prominent, indicating high hydration.
Texture: Leaves are turgid, crisp, and succulent.
Sensory Experience: The "cooling sensation" is explosive and immediate upon contact with the palate. The aroma is potent and volatile, filling the immediate area without needing to crush the leaves.
Flower State: Strictly vegetative (no flower spears), ensuring maximum oil concentration in the leaves.

Visual Appearance: Consistent dark green color. The purple/bronze blush is present but may be slightly less uniform or intense.
Structure: Leaves are intact and oval. Serrations are visible but may be slightly less sharp than the top tier.
Texture: Leaves are firm but may lack the ultimate "snap" of the Excellent grade.
Sensory Experience: Strong minty flavor and cooling sensation, though it may require slight chewing to fully activate the menthol experience.
Flower State: No flowers present.

Visual Appearance: Color is dulling to a matte green or olive. The purple/bronze blush may look muddy or brownish.
Structure: Leaves appear slightly flat (veining is less prominent) or are beginning to curl at the edges.
Texture: Leaves feel slightly limp or soft.
Sensory Experience: The cooling sensation is mild. The flavor is generally "minty" but lacks the sharp, herbaceous punch of high menthol content.
Flower State: Small flower buds (petite purple spears) are beginning to form, indicating the plant is shifting energy away from leaf oil production.

Visual Appearance: Visible yellowing (chlorosis) or brown spots on the leaf tips.
Structure: Leaves are shriveled, misshapen, or drooping significantly.
Texture: Leaves are leathery, dry, or tough.
Sensory Experience: Weak to no cooling effect. The flavor is grassy, hay-like, or slightly bitter.
Flower State: Full flowering spears are present and blooming.

Visual Appearance: Black, dark brown (necrosis), or grey slime on the leaves.
Texture: Mushy (wet rot) or crumbling into dust (desiccated).
Sensory Experience: Unpleasant aroma; smells musty, moldy, or like rotting vegetation (ammonia).
General: Evidence of insect infestation or foreign weeds mixed in.

Visual Appearance: Leaves are a vibrant, deep green with a clearly defined, sturdy purple stem. The tops consist of a perfect cluster of 3-4 twin leaflet pairs.
Texture: The "crinkled" texture is deep and distinct (bubbly appearance), indicating high hydration and freshness. Leaves are highly tender and succulent.
Structure: Leaves are turgid and upright, showing the "serrated edges" sharply. Dimensions are consistently within the 2–6 cm range.
Aroma: The aroma is potent and fills the immediate area without crushing.
Flavor/Sensation: The "cooling sensation" is immediate and intense upon tasting; the flavor is distinctly sweet.

Visual Appearance: Good green color. The stem is sturdy but may show a mix of green and purple (less distinct purple than the top tier).
Texture: Leaves are crinkled and tender, though perhaps slightly less "succulent" or thick than the Excellent grade.
Structure: Most tops have the 3-4 twin pairs, though some lower leaflets may be detached.
Aroma: Strong pleasant aroma, but requires slight agitation of the bunch to release the full profile.
Flavor/Sensation: Sweet and herbaceous, with a noticeable cooling effect.

Visual Appearance: Leaves appear a duller olive green. The stems are predominantly green or turning woody/brown, losing the characteristic purple hue.
Texture: Leaves appear flatter (loss of the crinkled texture) or slightly limp. They feel thin rather than succulent.
Structure: Tops look sparse (fewer than 3 twin pairs).
Aroma: The aroma is merely "minty" or grassy; the specific sweet/herbaceous complexity is weak.
Flavor/Sensation: The cooling sensation is mild or short-lived.

Visual Appearance: Visible yellowing (chlorosis) on the serrated edges. Stems are hard and woody.
Texture: Leaves are flaccid, wilting, or beginning to dry out (papery feel).
Structure: Significant physical damage (crushed leaves) or shriveling below the 2 cm minimum.
Aroma: Very faint scent, or a slight "hay-like" smell.
Flavor/Sensation: Flavor is flat or slightly bitter; no cooling sensation remains

Visual Appearance: Black, dark brown, or slimy leaves (necrosis/rot).
Texture: Mushy (wet rot) or crumbling dust (desiccated).
Structure: Stems are black or covered in mold.
Aroma: Unpleasant, sour, swampy, or smelling of ammonia.
General: Evidence of pests (holes in leaves) or foreign weeds.

Foliage Appearance: Leaves are vibrant, deep green, and highly turgid. The "wrinkled" texture is deep and distinct, indicating high water content. The "toothed" edges are sharp and crisp.
Stem Condition: Stems are green, succulent, and clearly square in cross-section. They support the bushy habit without bending.
Leaf Surface: Whether the specific variant is "smooth" or "hairy," the surface is clean and uniform. If hairy, the fuzz is soft, not matted.
Flower State: Ideally harvested before full bloom for culinary leaf quality. If flowers are present, they are tight, fresh white buds in the axils, not shedding.
Pests: Absolutely no insects present, despite being a "good nectar source.

Foliage Appearance: Consistent green color. Leaves are heart-shaped/oval but may be slightly less uniform in size.
Texture: The wrinkled surface is present, but leaves may feel slightly softer (less rigid) than the Excellent tier.
Stem Condition: Stems retain the square shape but may show signs of becoming fibrous near the base.
Flower State: Flowers may be open (pale yellow/purple) but look fresh and vibrant.
General: The bushy habit is preserved; the bunch does not look leggy.

Foliage Appearance: Leaves appear dull or olive-green. The "toothed" edges may be curling slightly.
Texture: Leaves feel flat (loss of the wrinkled 3D texture) or slightly dry/papery.
Stem Condition: Stems are becoming woody, tough, or turning brown.
Flower State: Flowers are fully open and beginning to brown or drop petals, making the clusters look messy.
General: The plant looks sparse, with more stem visible than leaf.

Foliage Appearance: Significant yellowing (chlorosis) or browning on the leaf tips.
Texture: Leaves are limp, flaccid, or leathery. The hairy varieties may feel dusty or rough.
Stem Condition: Stems are hard, woody sticks that snap dryly or bend without breaking (leathery).
Flower State: Flowers are dried out, brown, and seeding.
Aroma: (Implicit) Weak or hay-like smell replacing the fresh scent.

Foliage Appearance: Black, dark brown, or grey (mold).
Texture: Slimy/wet (rot) or crumbling into dust (desiccated).
Stem Condition: Black, moldy, or covered in webs.
General: Evidence of insect infestation (bees/bugs still attached) or foreign weeds mixed in.
Smell: Musty, mildewy, or sour.

Visual Appearance: Leaves are a deep, vibrant dark green with a distinct "silvery" sheen due to dense hairs (trichomes). No yellowing or browning is visible.
Texture: Leaves feel thick and velvety (fuzzy) to the touch. The oil glands are clearly visible under magnification as glistening dots.
Stem Content: Minimal stem presence. Any stems present are green, square, and tender, with no rigid woody sections.
Aroma: The aroma is explosive and immediate upon opening the sample. It is intensely earthy and pungent.
Flavor: The taste is sharply peppery and spicy, causing a slight numbing or warming sensation on the tongue (indicating high Carvacrol content >70%).

Visual Appearance: Leaves are consistent dark green but may lack the intense "silvery" overcast of the Excellent tier.
Texture: Leaves are intact and show the characteristic fuzzy texture, though perhaps slightly less dense.
Stem Content: Some small stems are visible, but they retain the square shape and are pliable, not brittle or hard.
Aroma: Strong and characteristic oregano scent, though it may take a moment to fill the immediate area.
Flavor: Distinctly earthy and savory. The "peppery" kick is present but smoother and less aggressive.

Visual Appearance: Color is a standard green, potentially dulling to olive. Some leaves may show purple tinges (acceptable but less desirable than the silvery-green for culinary uniformity).
Texture: Leaves may appear flatter or less fuzzy. Some fragmentation (broken leaves) is visible.
Stem Content: Noticeable presence of woody, rigid stems mixed with the leaves.
Aroma: The scent is herbal and grassy. The distinct "pizza herb" punch requires crushing the leaves to release.
Flavor: Flavor is mild and herbaceous. The specific high-Carvacrol "bite" is weak or absent.

Visual Appearance: Color is inconsistent, with yellow spots (chlorosis) or browning edges.
Texture: Leaves are dry, brittle, and shattering into dust. The oil glands appear dried out or empty.
Stem Content: High ratio of hard, round, woody branches to leaf material.
Flower Presence: Significant amount of flowering spikes included (which usually indicates the leaves have lost potency).
Aroma: Weak, hay-like, or smelling of dried straw rather than essential oils

Appearance (Leaves): Leaves are vibrant deep green and predominantly whole, clearly showcasing the characteristic "arrow shape."
Stem Content: Minimal presence of the "thin, stiff stems." The batch is almost entirely pure leaf material despite the natural sparse growth pattern.
Aroma: The aroma is intense and pungent. The complex top notes of citrus (lime-like) and mild licorice are immediately detectable and distinct above the earthy base.
Flavor: Flavor is robust and bold—significantly more intense than standard oregano. The citrus zest note is bright on the palate.
Flowers: If present, flower petals are bright white and dried naturally, adding aesthetic contrast without looking brown/dead.

Appearance (Leaves): Color is a consistent green but may lack the deep vibrancy of the top tier.
Structure: Most leaves are intact, though some tips of the "arrows" may be broken.
Stem Content: Low stem content, but small fragments of the stiff stems are visible upon close inspection.
Aroma: Strong traditional oregano scent. The citrus and licorice notes are present but require crushing the leaves to fully release.
Flavor: Intense and savory, though the complex "high notes" (citrus/licorice) are slightly muted compared to the Excellent grade

Appearance (Leaves): Leaves appear dull green or olive-colored. The "arrow shape" is difficult to distinguish because the leaves are fragmented or crushed.

Aroma: Smells like generic dried herbs. The specific citrus and licorice nuances are lost or very faint; smells more like hay or dried grass
Flavor: The intensity is average. It tastes like oregano but lacks the "bit more intense" punch described in the ideal state.
Flowers: Flower remnants are beige or browning

Appearance (Leaves): Significant yellowing or browning. The batch looks "stemmy" (high ratio of stiff stems to leaf material).

Flavor: Flat and weak. The distinctive phytochemical profile is undetectable; barely distinguishable from generic weed/brush.

Structure: Stems are populated with leaves similar to Tsuga needles, showing no gaps.

Dimensions: Shriveled needles significantly smaller than the descriptions.
Structure: Sparse branches where leaves have dropped, leaving only woody stems.

Appearance (Leaves): Leaves are a vibrant green with a distinct "semi-glossy" sheen. They are perfectly lanceolate with sharp, defined tapered points.
Texture: Leaves are highly pliable (flexible without breaking). Stems are pale green and snap cleanly, exhibiting the ideal "crisp" consistency without being stringy.
Aroma: The anise aroma is potent and fresh immediately upon handling.
Flavor: The flavor is complex and balanced; the "bittersweet" and "acidic" base is elevated by clear, distinguishable notes of sweet vanilla and mint.
Flowers: If present, flowers are fresh, bright (white/yellow/green), and turgid.

Appearance (Leaves): Good green color, though the "semi-glossy" finish may be slightly dulled to a satin finish.
Texture: Leaves remain pliable. Stems are green but may be slightly more fibrous than the 'Excellent' tier (requiring a bit more chewing).
Aroma: Strong licorice/anise scent is present, though it may not fill the room instantly.
Flavor: The primary licorice and fennel notes are strong. The subtle "sweet vanilla" nuance is faint or difficult to detect.
Flowers: Flowers are intact but may look slightly weary or less vibrant in color.

Appearance (Leaves): Leaves appear matte (loss of gloss) or a dull olive green.
Texture: Leaves are slightly drooping or limp (loss of turgidity). They may fold rather than holding their shape.
Stem Condition: Stems are becoming tough or woody at the base, losing their "crisp" quality. They bend rather than snap.
Aroma: The aroma is generic "green herb" or grassy. The anise character is weak and requires crushing the leaf to detect.
Flavor: The flavor is predominantly acidic or bitter; the sweet/minty nuances are largely absent.

Appearance (Leaves): Visible yellowing at the tips or edges. Leaves may be curling or drying out.
Texture: Leathery or dry. The "thin" leaves feel papery.
Stem Condition: Stems are hard, woody, and pale/whitish (over-mature).
Aroma: Very faint scent, or a slight "hay-like" smell replaces the fresh anise aroma.
Flavor: Flavor is flat, strictly bitter, or metallic. No licorice sweetness remains.

Appearance (Leaves): Black, dark brown, or slimy (decomposition).
Texture: Mushy/slimy (rot) or crumbling into dust (desiccated).
Stem Condition: Stems are black or covered in mold.
Aroma: Unpleasant, musty, moldy, or smelling of ammonia/rot.
Flavor: Rancid and inedible

Appearance (Leaves): Leaves are vibrant, deep green, and stand upright. The "wispy" structure is distinct and separated, not clumped.
Appearance (Flowers): If flowering, the umbels are bright yellow and intact, forming a perfect flat-topped cluster.
Aroma: Pungent, fresh, and zesty. The sour, pickle-like scent is immediately apparent without crushing.
Flavor: Complex and potent. The notes of anise, celery, and the lemon finish are perfectly balanced and distinct.
Texture: Turgid and crisp; stems snap easily.

Appearance (Leaves): Green color is consistent but may lack the intense sheen of the 'Excellent' grade.
Appearance (Flowers): Flowers are yellow but may show very slight wilting at the edges of the cluster.
Aroma: Strong characteristic aroma, though it may require slight handling to release the full bouquet.
Flavor: The anise and parsley notes are clear, though the lemon finish might be slightly less sharp.
Texture: Mostly crisp, though the fern-like leaves may be slightly softer.

Appearance (Leaves): Leaves appear dull green. There is no yellowing, but the "wispy" leaves may be slightly matted or drooping.
Appearance (Flowers): Flowers appear faded yellow or are beginning to drop petals.
Aroma: The fresh sour scent is weak; smells more generally "grassy" or herbaceous than distinctively like dill.
Flavor: Flavor is present but mild; the specific notes (anise/lemon) are difficult to distinguish individually.
Texture: Leaves are limp or beginning to wilt; stems bend rather than snap.

Appearance (Leaves): Visible yellowing on the tips of the fern-like leaves. The plant looks tired.
Appearance (Flowers): Umbels are browning or drying out significantly.
Aroma: Very faint scent, or a slight "hay-like" or dried smell replacing the fresh aroma.
Flavor: Flavor is flat and weak. The lemon finish is entirely absent.
Texture: Flaccid and limp. The wispy structure has collapsed.

Appearance (Leaves): Dark, black, or slimy leaves. significant decomposition or browning.
Appearance (Flowers): Brown, shriveled, or rot evident in the flower clusters.
Aroma: Unpleasant, musty, or smelling of decay/rot rather than fresh pickles.
Flavor: Unpalatable, bitter, or rancid.
Texture: Slimy, mushy, or completely dried out and brittle (depending on storage conditions).

Foliage Appearance: Leaves are a vibrant, uniform gray-green with the paler underside clearly visible. The "revolute" (rolled under) edges are distinct and tight.

Stem Condition: Stems are predominantly green, square, and pliable. The woody brownish-purple base is minimal or trimmed away.
Aroma: The aroma is potent immediately upon opening the sample. The complex bouquet of mint, lemon, and the specific "peppery warmth" is distinct.
Flower Condition: If harvested in bloom, flowers are fresh, brightly colored (pink/lavender), and intact
